State of AI Data Labs and Human Feedback

An expanded evidence-linked analyst report on suppliers, supervision, datasets, benchmarks and buyer decisions

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

This comprehensive synthesis covers the selected approved corpus of 73 qualifying supplier groups, 225 distinct reviewed paper works, 85 dataset families and 87 benchmark families. Twelve chapters connect disclosed offerings and delivery roles, technical methods, human operations, commercial units, rights and security with ten original proposed buyer pilots and explicit acceptance conditions. The bounded eligible core contains 416 source-qualified identities, with 389 deeply dispositioned (93.5096%); 102 named Unknown targets and unresolved discovery and family-identity capacities remain retained. The accepted finite 200-hypothesis reference audit and the separate screening requirement are distinct quality gates. Publication and archival status are reported separately from source and review dates. Separate AI review is not human peer review; this report claims neither a market census nor independently measured provider performance.

AI-assisted research with Separate AI review. Each approved assertion carries exact-content author, source-verifier and adversarial source-content receipts; original reading scopes, source dates, review dates and qualifications remain unchanged. This revision synthesizes 57 additional family records from the approved graph without new primary-source retrieval, source-content approval, experiment reproduction, supplier operations audit or rights certification. Report-level evidence-auditor and adversarial receipts identify their actual scope, exact report and graph digests, and review dates; an approval applies only to its matching content. Separate AI review does not imply human peer review.

1. Executive assessment

Method

ScienceToStartup publishes State of AI Data Labs and Human Feedback under the publisher identity Musa Ozdem. It is an evidence-linked analyst synthesis for buyers, research teams and contributors. Publication status, exact-edition citations and verified archive links are reported separately from the captured-source cutoff and substantive review dates. A scheduled date or a prepared package does not establish archival publication, and no human peer review is claimed. The source-qualified eligible core is frozen at 416 identities; the actual reference audit is accepted, while publication separately requires screening and all other gates. Canonical dataset 2.5.0 and historical source/review dates are unchanged. The purpose is to expose the source observation, the analyst’s reasoning, its confidence and the evidence that would change it.

Method

The current authoring input contains 2,548 approved assertions, 73 qualifying supplier groups, 225 distinct reviewed paper works, 85 dataset families and 87 benchmark families under coverage method 1.3.0. All 39 legacy organizations have completed bounded inclusion audits; 38 have conclusive dispositions and BenchFlow remains commercially pending. The graph retains 195 candidate and 39 historical assertions. Candidate records include unresolved or superseded material; their count is not a scientific-error count. These are selected-corpus counts. Within the separately source-qualified 416-unit frozen core, 389 are deeply dispositioned: 389/416 = 93.5096%, leaving 27 genuine deep-review gaps. This report covers every counted paper work and supplier group and all counted families without claiming a census; the methods preserve the full unresolved scope.

Analysis

The market is more intelligible when the comparison begins with the unit being bought. A participant platform, a managed annotation program, a licensed dataset, an evaluation service and an executable RL environment leave different responsibilities with the buyer. Prolific distinguishes participant access from managed collection; Snorkel describes refreshed non-exclusive products; Mercor describes expert task construction; Surge describes environments and verifiers. The analytical implication is to compare statements of work and accepted deliverables before comparing brand claims. This evidence supports a responsibility map within this sample, rather than a universal competitive ranking.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.task-construction, candidate.supplier.surge_ai.rl-environments

Analysis

The word human conceals several different supervision arrangements. Human-written source material, human task design, independently collected judgments, correction of model drafts and human review of a model-selected subset are not interchangeable inputs. HelpSteer3, UltraFeedback, FineWeb-Edu and the described DeepSeek-R1 cold-start process demonstrate distinct combinations. A buyer should ask where a person intervenes and what that person can observe. Nothing in this sample establishes that one provenance class always produces better models; the defensible comparison is whether the supervision target and validation design fit the intended task.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback, candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels, cohort5.claim.deepseekr1.human-coldstart

Analysis

Quality requires denominators and a theory of disagreement. HelpSteer3’s retained consensus, HelpSteer2’s closest-rating aggregation, InstructGPT’s ranked sets and DICES’ repeated safety judgments arise from different observation processes. A pair count can expand from rankings without adding independent people; a post-filter agreement result can improve while excluding difficult items; a majority can erase a meaningful minority. Procurement should preserve raw labels, exclusions and adjudication reasons. These are methodological judgments based on the documented workflows, not measured differences in supplier performance.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus, next.claim.helpsteer2.qa, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets, cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference

Analysis

Executable outcomes improve observability but do not eliminate judgment. SWE-bench tests, OSWorld state checks, τ-bench database rewards and PaperBench rubric leaves expose concrete success conditions. Their papers also identify incomplete test coverage, damaging side effects, missed policy violations or judge limitations. A reliable acceptance plan therefore needs both outcome checks and a separate review of constraints, side effects and ambiguous failures. The evidence does not justify treating a passed verifier as a certification of deployment readiness or general professional competence.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring, cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap, cohort4.claim.taubench.reward-limit, cohort6.claim.paperbench.judge-validation

Analysis

Public financial and workforce numbers answer different questions. Appen’s annual group revenue, Proximal’s annualized pace, Scale’s cumulative contributor payout and Prolific’s active-participant disclosure do not form a common revenue, capacity or labor denominator. Labelbox financing combines equity and a credit facility. The report therefore offers a commercial evidence ledger and project-cost methodology rather than market-share estimates or a valuation league table. Missing disclosure remains unknown, and a large advertised pool does not establish current paid availability for a particular language, credential or task.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025, repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout, repair20261111.claim.current-reference221, candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing

Analysis

Rights, privacy and security must follow the exact material and service boundary. Marketplace terms, a website privacy notice, a training-data license, a worker agreement and a security attestation can cover different subjects. Defined.ai separates marketplace datasets from new collection; AfterQuery excludes customer processor work from its website policy; Mercor directs work-platform users to a separate notice; MathVista retains underlying image and question rights while restricting training use. The analyst judgment is to obtain project-specific evidence for each boundary. Public documentation completeness is useful for diligence, but it is not itself a quality or compliance rating.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.marketplace-separation, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.processor-privacy-boundary, candidate.supplier.mercor.privacy-scope, cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms

Method

All nine executive finding identifiers from the previous unpublished synthesis are retained. The additional studies refine their evidence and limits: post-selection agreement differs from raw agreement; model-simulated feedback differs from live expert assistance; disclosure audits describe reporting; and observed costs depend on the counted work and time. These refinements do not create a published weekly comparison or rewrite a historical archive. Confidence remains attached to each scoped judgment and to the evidence that could change it.

Analysis

The added annotation studies strengthen a practical distinction between an improved retained dataset and an improved production process. HelpSteer2 raises agreement after selecting and filtering labels; the surgical-annotation study compares instruction conditions and subsequent QA; LabelAId measures a particular intervention against researcher-adjudicated labels. Those designs answer different questions. A buyer should require raw-input, excluded-item and final-acceptance denominators, plus independent error inspection, before interpreting a high agreement score or a QA stage as evidence of better delivered work.

Evidence: cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection, cohort9.claim.qualityassured.qa-result, cohort9.claim.qualityassured.limits-identity, cohort9.claim.labelaid.adjudication-study, cohort9.claim.labelaid.precision-time

Analysis

The added professional-work literature strengthens a measurement warning rather than a labor forecast. APEX-Agents distinguishes any-attempt and all-attempt success; APEX-Accounting contrasts mean criterion completion with all-eight-attempt reliability; DAYJOB separates strict pass from relaxed thresholds and reports creator-estimated healthcare time with a separately described finance mean; PLE combines rubric and hybrid executable scores. These are different questions about selected tasks. Confidence is high that their percentages cannot be pooled into a share of jobs automated. A useful buyer comparison requires a common task population, complete-attempt accounting, independently calibrated judges and observed practitioner baselines.

Analytical judgment

delivery-unit-before-provider

In this reviewed sample, a useful supplier comparison begins with the delivery unit: participant access, licensed data, custom tasks or executable environments.

Buyer implication
Specify who owns task design, annotation, QA, rights clearance and acceptance before comparing proposals.
Limitations
First-party offering descriptions do not establish interchangeable services, capacity, realized quality or a market-wide supplier ranking.
Confidence
Moderate for this sample’s disclosed distinctions; low for prevalence outside it.
Reasoning
Prolific distinguishes participant access and managed collection; Snorkel describes refreshed non-exclusive products; Mercor describes custom task construction; Surge offers environments and verifiers. Their responsibilities differ even where capability labels overlap. The expanded corpus also distinguishes engineering teams, managed evaluation, hosted compute and contract-limited talent acquisition; the comparison remains task-specific. The current supplier set also contains schema-mapped web feeds and a Datatang/Nexdata group combining licensed resources and customization. A group identity is not proof that every brand or service is interchangeable.
What would change this assessment
Matched statements of work and independently checked deliveries could show that particular offerings meet the same requirement and permit narrower outcome comparisons.

Analytical judgment

human-and-model-provenance

Human content, human labels and human oversight are distinct provenance claims; the selected datasets contain materially different combinations.

Buyer implication
Require a stage-level provenance manifest and test the label target relevant to the intended task.
Limitations
The reviewed methods are source-reported and version-specific. No universal advantage of human or synthetic labels is established. Human review of a model draft does not establish wholly human authorship, and synthetic provenance does not establish inferior or superior quality.
Confidence
High for the documented provenance distinctions; unestablished for comparative training outcomes.
Reasoning
HelpSteer3 describes independent human preference annotations, UltraFeedback describes GPT-4 labels and FineWeb-Edu describes model-scored educational filtering. Calling these one annotation category would erase the origin of the supervision signal. The expanded methods also include human correction of model responses and model-generated process signals, reinforcing stage-level provenance. StarCoder separates human PII annotation from code-corpus content; the rubric study separates human taxonomy development from model-persona scoring. These additions strengthen stage-level rather than binary provenance. CharXiv separates model suggestions from human selection; ProgramBench separates source-visible construction agents from source-hidden reconstruction; GeneBench-Pro reports simulated problem creation with AI assistance and author oversight. Provenance must follow each stage.
What would change this assessment
Independent task-matched validation with raw annotations and generation logs could support outcome comparisons or expose errors in the reported provenance.

Analytical judgment

agreement-needs-denominators

Released agreement and preference-pair totals cannot be interpreted without the independent-judgment and exclusion denominators.

Buyer implication
Request raw-to-retained counts, invalid-item rules, repeat labels, disagreement slices and corrected acceptance.
Limitations
The reviewed workflows differ in task and sampling. They cannot rank provider quality, and no common reliability measurement was executed.
Confidence
High for the methodological distinction; low for transferring a numerical agreement result between workflows.
Reasoning
HelpSteer3’s retained consensus, HelpSteer2’s post-filter closest-rating aggregation, InstructGPT’s ranked sets and DICES’ repeated judgments have different observation and selection denominators. The added HelpSteer2 paper makes the exclusions explicit; the inference study limits normalized scores to within-pair comparisons; Gilardi excludes trained-rater disagreement from the accuracy reference. These distinctions make raw counts, exclusions and adjudication necessary before comparison. MACE reports coverage-dependent comparisons, MMRB2 excludes ambiguous pairs and Regulated Advice Bench retains translated rows under one original-item label. None is an independent-judgment count merely because it has many rows. The added sources also distinguish nested chart questions, predefined consensus criteria from individualized rubrics, and sampled judge agreement from review of every response. Source-stage headcount discrepancies remain unresolved.
What would change this assessment
A common held-out task with independent raw judgments and the same exclusion rules could make reliability comparisons meaningful.

Analytical judgment

artifact-role-is-narrow

Named artifact attribution is strongest when it preserves the exact contribution stage and release rather than extending a brand association across a family.

Buyer implication
Ask for source-supported roles for the specific delivered artifact; keep recruitment, annotation, validation and authorship separate.
Limitations
These examples do not reveal contract values, contribution shares, exhaustive supplier lists or causal provider performance.
Confidence
High for the explicit scoped roles in this sample; incomplete for the broader supplier graph.
Reasoning
HelpSteer3 names Scale and Translated for different subsets; the Prolific case establishes recruitment through a researcher-owned interface; U-MATH credits Toloka AI and Gradarius with validation of professor-authored problems. These relationships support narrower claims than sole production. The added papers document contractor demonstrations/comparisons, a PII-labeling project and expert benchmark construction as separate roles. The report does not extend them into complete corpus authorship or a causal provider-performance claim. CVDP thanks Turing for dataset collaboration and Cadence for tool licenses; SUPERChem names original-problem and compute contributors; HCAST identifies affiliated individuals’ QA roles. These are different contributions and do not imply complete corpus ownership or an unstated organizational supply contract.
What would change this assessment
Additional artifact-specific acknowledgments, contributor records or contracts could establish further stages or revise the scope.

Analytical judgment

benchmark-protocol-before-score

Benchmark family names alone are insufficient for comparing scores or deciding deployment readiness.

Buyer implication
Freeze task version, candidate responses, aggregation and execution environment, then inspect errors on the buyer’s actual task.
Limitations
No benchmark was executed for this report. The reviewed sources do not establish a universal deployment-quality ranking. Reported task, release, harness, attempt budget and uncertainty conventions differ; unresolved source counts are not silently reconciled.
Confidence
High for protocol differences and stated limitations; unestablished for any new system’s performance.
Reasoning
RewardBench versions change scoring structure; TruthfulQA changes answer protocol and separates generation metrics; SWE-bench warns that passing tests does not ensure complete, efficient or readable solutions. The measures answer different questions. OSWorld and τ-bench additionally identify outcome-checking gaps for damaging side effects and policy violations. The new professional suites distinguish repeated any/all success, criterion averages, strict/relaxed passes and hybrid scores. They cannot be pooled into a professional-capability percentage or a job-automation rate. The added evidence spans median-of-three criterion scores, equal-task all-field pass rates with hierarchical bootstrap, and fitted human-time horizons over overlapping task inputs. Release revisions and source discrepancies remain part of the measurement definition.
What would change this assessment
Reproducible matched-protocol results and independently checked target-task outcomes could support a narrower comparative claim.

Analytical judgment

commercial-denominators-stay-separate

The selected commercial disclosures cannot be combined into supplier market shares, production-capacity rankings or a common unit-cost comparison.

Buyer implication
Retain period, currency, organizational scope, active-window definition and acceptance basis; obtain a project-specific quote and availability check.
Limitations
Coverage is selected and incomplete. Missing disclosure is unknown, not zero; the observed figures are not matched measures.
Confidence
High for the incompatibility of these disclosed denominators; no confidence claim is made about market-wide shares.
Reasoning
Appen reports full-year consolidated and geographic-segment revenue, Scale reports cumulative contributor payouts with unspecified period and dollar currency, and Prolific distinguishes active participants from a waitlist without defining the active window. None supplies a matched current paid-work or human-data revenue denominator across suppliers. Proximal’s annualized disclosure and Labelbox’s mixed financing add further incompatible commercial measures. Datatang’s unaudited six-month group revenue and HCAST’s task-specific human incentive schedule add useful but unmatched commercial units. Neither supplies a current common service price or a supplier-capacity denominator.
What would change this assessment
Comparable segment accounts, audited activity windows and accepted-unit cost records across the same scope could permit limited financial or operational comparisons.

Analytical judgment

multilingual-intersections-before-language-counts

Multilingual suitability depends on language-domain-task intersections and native validity, rather than a language count alone.

Buyer implication
Specify every required intersection, preserve translation/review provenance and calibrate the judge in the target locale.
Limitations
These selected studies do not establish universal translation inferiority, global language coverage or a provider ranking.
Confidence
Moderate for these documented methodological distinctions; unmeasured for current supplier performance.
Reasoning
HelpSteer3 records missing intersections, M-IFEval changes language-inappropriate constraints, BenchMAX post-edits translations and MENLO measures localized dimensions. JEEM’s local dialect judgments and StereoTales’ narrower human reference panel expose different language-generation and normative-validation boundaries. Prompt translation, chemical image-to-text parity and culturally bounded harmfulness judgments are different validation problems. StereoTales also retains an unresolved agreement/acceptability wording-direction conflict, so its correlation is not treated as universal normative validity.
What would change this assessment
Matched native-authored, translated and post-edited task studies with independent target-locale evaluation could narrow or revise the judgment.

Analytical judgment

rights-follow-exact-material-and-service

Rights, privacy and security diligence must follow exact components, services and uses rather than a top-level policy or license label.

Buyer implication
Obtain component rights and the actual project processing/security scope before accepting data or environments.
Limitations
This is public-source evidence and methodological judgment, not legal advice, rights clearance or an assurance audit.
Confidence
High for the documented scope differences; unestablished for legal compliance of particular deployments.
Reasoning
AlpacaEval separates code/data terms, RewardBench retains component obligations, MathVista restricts training use and provider notices distinguish website from customer processing. Magpie retains conflicting/source-specific declarations, StarCoder retains detection/opt-out limits and Chartography distinguishes online provenance from redistribution permission. A public-data collection policy does not establish downstream rights; CVDP has component-specific declarations and unspecified entries; GeneBench-Pro’s paper and public package make different declarations for different objects.
What would change this assessment
Project-specific agreements, rights-holder permissions and independent scoped assurance evidence could resolve particular unknowns.

Analytical judgment

verifiable-outcomes-need-side-effect-review

Executable success checks should be paired with independent review of constraints, side effects and verifier error.

Buyer implication
Test valid alternatives, plausible shortcuts, harmful extra actions and infrastructure failures in the acceptance pilot.
Limitations
No environment or provider was independently executed for this report, and no failure-prevalence estimate is claimed.
Confidence
High for the stated benchmark limitations; unmeasured for any new buyer deployment.
Reasoning
SWE-bench passing tests do not guarantee a complete solution; OSWorld identifies damaging-side-effect gaps; τ-bench notes missed policy violations; MBPP documents assertion gaming. PivotRL local checks, HANDBOOK.md prohibited-state criteria and PLE’s hybrid gate show why check coverage and final-task safety require separate inspection. Finite behavioral tests, no-op mutants and reference-isolated grading need independent falsification. Judge/verifier disagreement remains a disagreement measure rather than a human-verified error rate.
What would change this assessment
A matched evaluation showing that the project verifier reliably detects the buyer’s critical constraints could narrow the need for additional manual review in that scope.
